## Summary

A visitor reported sending a gesto ("Paloma de paz") that showed up in the Recuerdos feed with a raw UUID-looking internal ID (e.g. `c7283d90-d4cf-4f90-8fdb-66ea1c9f127c`) instead of its description ("Que descanse en paz"), and the wrong/missing emoji (a generic 💐 default instead of 🕊️).

I traced the frontend send path (`enviarGesto` → `confirmarGesto`) and it correctly sends the article's real `emoji` and `descripcion` text to the backend when a gesture is sent — so the corruption happens on the backend side (the Google Apps Script connected to `API_URL`), most likely a column mismatch when writing/reading the "gesto" record (e.g. the record's own ID landing in the description column, and the emoji column ending up empty, hence the 💐 fallback). That backend code lives outside this repository (hosted on script.google.com), so I can't fix the root cause here.

What I *did* fix: `publica/pagina.html` was rendering whatever the backend returned as the gesto's description with no validation, so a corrupted record leaked a raw internal ID to visitors. Added a small guard (`pareceIdInterno`) that detects a UUID-shaped value and, in that case, simply omits the description line instead of displaying it. Verified with a mocked API response reproducing the exact corrupted shape from the report — the feed now shows just the sender's name and emoji, no leaked ID.

I also reviewed the credits purchase flow (the "paquetes" grid → `selPaquete()` → `crearSesionCreditos` → Stripe redirect) since it was flagged for a check. The frontend logic itself looks correct: it sends `creditos`/`precio`/`servicioId`/`email`, redirects to `resp.urlPago` on success, and shows an error toast + resets the button on failure. I could not exercise a live Stripe checkout end-to-end from this sandboxed environment (no network access to script.google.com or Stripe here), so that still needs a real test by someone with access to the live backend/Stripe account.

## Scope

Destructive convergence and optimization of the Rust/Hugging Face execution path after the minimal JSON-contract migration.

This PR intentionally removes legacy Rust candidate metadata/run-context construction and replaces it with generated contracts produced by the canonical Python orchestration layer. It will also harden Cargo reproducibility, session/provider configuration, audio resampling, CI/E2E coverage, and HF Bucket write semantics.

## First implementation slice

- Rust no longer reads human-authored `metadata.json.runtime_contract`.
- Python emits a generated candidate execution contract after strict candidate inspection.
- Rust re-verifies artifact SHA-256, sizes, bundle SHA, tokenizer paths, and CTC runtime bindings.
- `runtime.json` is mandatory in the Rust revision loader.
- canonical run-context generation moves to Python; the old Rust run-context builder is removed.
- ORT inputs use named bindings and borrowed `TensorRef` values.
- CTC logits are decoded from the borrowed ORT output view without cloning the full logits tensor.
- linear audio resampling is replaced by an anti-aliasing polyphase windowed-sinc implementation.
- Rust benchmark candidate identity is aligned to the candidate bundle SHA expected by promotion.

Further commits in this PR will finish lockfile/`--locked`, workflow migration, provider tuning/telemetry, HF write-once/plan behavior, and E2E tests.

body:
Round two of the Windows screenshots. The first round is technically correct and stays useful as evidence in issues, but it is weak at the top of a README and in the marketplace carousel.

## What was wrong with round one

The strongest of the three showed `MARK=box7` and `echo sandbox:$MARK:$(pwd)`. Two tool calls, an empty sidebar, no metrics line. It works as evidence only for someone who already knows why persistence matters on Windows. To a passer by it is two meaningless variable names.

Looking at what the high-star repos in this ecosystem actually ship, the pattern is consistent. Real work in a real project, ten or more tool calls, a visible metrics line, and the whole window including the sidebar rather than a cropped chat panel.

## What these show

**Sandboxed preset.** A whole bug fix at `workspace-write`. The agent runs `node test.js`, sees the assertion fail, reads `index.js`, finds `sub` written as `a + b`, rewrites it to `a - b`, and runs again for `all tests passed`. Six steps. The frame carries the preset name, the `Workspace Write` badge, the session list, and the metrics line reading `1 turns · 6 steps | Tool call 1m16s | 136 tok/s | Cache hit 89% | Input 11.5K tok`.

Verified on disk after the run.

```
$ cat index.js
function sub(a, b) { return a - b }
$ node test.js
all tests passed   # exit 0
```

**Git Bash preset.** Persistence proved inside real work rather than with a marker. `export BUILD=v1` finishes in one tool call. The next separate tool call runs `git init`, `git add`, and `git commit -m "$BUILD"`, and the commit lands as `v1` because the variable survived. `git log --oneline` prints `d812072 (HEAD -> master) v1`.

The first attempt at this shot failed in an instructive way. Asked as a single message, the agent chained everything into one `cd && export && git init && git commit` call, which proves nothing about persistence. Splitting it into two messages is what makes the claim real.

**Preset picker.** Same content, larger crop, so the two Minimal rows and their bilingual descriptions stay readable when the carousel scales the image to 150px tall.

**market-card.png** becomes the sandboxed shot. It was a rendered composite before.

## Sizing

All four are 1456x840, ratio 1.7333. The carousel renders `height:150px` with `max-width:260px`, so the box width follows the image ratio up to 260. At 1.7333 the box is exactly 260 by 150 and nothing is cropped. Measured by rendering the actual CSS rather than by calculation.

| ratio | rendered box | crop |
|---|---|---|
| 1.5000 | 225.0x150.0 | none |
| 1.7333 | 260.0x150.0 | none |
| 1.7778 | 260.0x150.0 | 20px each side |
| 2.4000 | 260.0x150.0 | 267px each side |

Anything at or below 1.7333 is safe. Above it, the sides go.

## Not included

No annotation boxes yet. The two spots worth circling are the `Workspace Write` badge in the sandboxed shot and the `d812072 ... v1` line in the Git Bash shot.

# PR Description

## Summary

Adds reusable-geometry studies for discrete plane-wave and RCS simulations.

The new `PlaneWaveStudy`:

- supports angle-, vector-, and axial-defined discrete plane waves;
- permits per-case direction, polarisation, waveform, timing, and amplitude scaling;
- reuses the main Yee geometry;
- rebuilds direction-dependent DPW grids and their PML state for every case;
- resets and recompiles declarative KSIR/NTFF accumulators and incident-field normalization;
- supports both Python API and CSV/hash-command workflows;
- stores requested and actual rationalised plane-wave parameters in HDF5;
- rejects additional excitations that would make RCS normalization ambiguous;
- allows passive subgrids enclosed by the TFSF and NTFF surfaces.

NTFF plane-wave metadata is now also written into the frequency-transform output group.

## Motivation

Angular and polarization sweeps previously required rebuilding the entire model. Simply retaining the existing plane-wave object is unsafe because its auxiliary grid, integer propagation mapping, material profile, projections, PML state, and incident-field DFT depend on the selected direction.

This implementation retains only the direction-independent Yee geometry and reconstructs all dependent source and NTFF state.

Le collecteur lit des **valeurs de retour**. Un test interdit `generate_program`, `planner_candidate_pool`, `substitution` et `_rank_zone` dans son source — il ne peut pas re-décider.

## OQ tranchées et appliquées

| OQ | Résolution |
|---|---|
| **1 rétention** | `RETENTION_POLICY_V1 = OWNER_LIFETIME` — aucun TTL, aucune purge, aucun archivage |
| **2 alternatives** | Persistées **seulement** si le moteur les connaissait ⇒ **`[]` partout aujourd'hui**, jamais reconstruites |
| **3 historique** | **Immuable** — écouteur `before_update` qui **lève**, pas une convention d'appelant |
| **4 granularité** | Une trace = une décision sémantique · `CONTRIBUTION_CREDIT` **agrégé par zone** · morphologie **non persistée** |

## Où l'observation se déclenche

À la **matérialisation** (l'utilisateur agit), jamais au rendu de `/programs` : y écrire un groupe de traces à chaque affichage de page est exactement ce que le brief interdit pour la récupération et la morphologie.

Le chemin produit reste **littéralement inchangé** — le budget est re-dérivé dans l'observateur (pur et déterministe) plutôt que de restructurer l'appel qui produit le plan. C'est ce qui rend la preuve de retirabilité crédible.

## Un défaut réel trouvé par mes propres tests

`test_a_collector_failure_does_not_break_materialization` a **échoué au premier passage**. L'observateur avale bien ses erreurs, mais **le site d'appel n'était pas protégé** : le jour où quelqu'un modifie l'observateur et le laisse lever, la route rendrait **500 alors que le brouillon est déjà créé et valide**. Une garantie qui dépend de la discipline interne de l'appelé n'en est pas une. La route porte désormais sa propre garde.

## Deux gardes écrites/renforcées AVANT de pouvoir planter

- **`basis` verbatim n'était pas gardé du tout** — rien ne comparait le `basis` persisté à celui du moteur. Test écrit d'abord, avec un compteur qui échoue si aucune comparaison n'a lieu (sinon il passerait à vide).
- **La retirabilité ne couvrait que la mémoire** — le test central planifie depuis des préférences en mémoire, donc un collecteur réécrivant les préférences **persistées** serait passé au travers. Un second test planifie des deux côtés **via la base**. C'est lui, et lui seul, qui attrape la plantation 3.

## Les cinq plantations exigées — toutes mordent

| # | Plantation | Garde qui tombe |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | aplatir les sources en une colonne | `test_source_classes_stay_separate_in_storage` |
| 2 | réécrire le `basis` | `test_the_basis_is_cited_verbatim_never_reworded` |
| 3 | muter les entrées persistées | `test_observation_does_not_mutate_the_persisted_decision_inputs` |
| 4 | `UPDATE` historique | `test_a_persisted_trace_cannot_be_updated` |
| 5 | alternative fabriquée | `test_rejected_alternatives_are_empty_...` |

## Retirabilité — preuve centrale

Avec collecteur vs **entièrement désactivé** : budget, empreinte de plan, prescriptions, contributions, replan, matérialisation, descripteurs morphologiques — **identiques**. Le test vérifie d'abord que le collecteur a réellement tourné, sans quoi il ne prouverait rien. Les quatre moteurs purs conservent **exactement** leurs paramètres, sans `db` ni `user_id`.

## Preuves

| | |
|---|---|
| Tests dédiés | **30** |
| Balayage ciblé | **254** |
| Full sweep local | **4 451** |
| Drift / roundtrip | OK / 48 objets identiques |
| Budget ruff | 536 ≤ 548 |
| Pré-scan Sonar | S9073 **0**, S1192 **0** |

## Limites énoncées

- **Aucune alternative rejetée disponible** — les producteurs ne conservent pas leurs classements. `[]` est la réponse honnête ; une tranche d'instrumentation dédiée serait nécessaire.
- `REPLAN_DELTA` et `RECOVERY_ASSESSMENT` **pas encore écrits** : leur frontière de consommation est le replan, non branché ici.
- `MEASURED_FACT` / `DERIVED_FACT` n'ont pas de colonne dédiée et rejoignent `constraint_sources` ; leur `kind` reste intact, donc la nature n'est jamais perdue.

**Morphologie → influence planificateur : TOUJOURS DÉSACTIVÉE.**

body:
## What changed

- Removed the `myeventlane_launch` decorator that read unsigned Stripe event IDs before authentication.
- Removed request-local retry and key-value processed markers from the launch module.
- Restored direct webhook ownership to `myeventlane_admin_dashboard`, where Stripe signature verification occurs before dispatch.
- Added regression tests for missing and forged signatures, ownership order, and duplicate paid-transfer handling.

## Why

The launch decorator trusted an event ID from an unsigned payload and marked any response below 500 as processed. An invalid-signature 400 response could therefore poison the duplicate marker for a legitimate later delivery with the same event ID. It also retried the webhook handler three times within one request.

## Impact

Invalid webhook payloads cannot reach payout-ledger processing or create a processed marker. Valid retries are handled by Stripe, while the existing payout-ledger mutation guard keeps duplicate `transfer.paid` deliveries harmless.

## Validation

- PHPUnit: 5 tests, 21 assertions passed.
- Drupal Check/PHPStan: no errors for the launch module and focused authentication test.
- PHP syntax and Git whitespace checks passed.
- No real payment, payout, webhook delivery, database change or configuration import was performed.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes payout webhook security boundaries and removes idempotency/retry logic; incorrect behavior could affect ledger reconciliation or allow/block legitimate Stripe retries.
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes the **myeventlane_launch** Stripe payout webhook decorator and its **StripeWebhookProcessor** (key-value “processed” markers, in-request retries, and event-ID extraction from unsigned bodies). Payout webhooks are handled only by **myeventlane_admin_dashboard**’s `StripeWebhookController`, where signature verification runs before dispatch and ledger updates.
> 
> Adds regression coverage: unit tests that missing/invalid signatures return 400 without touching the database, contract tests that launch no longer decorates the webhook, and that the owner verifies signatures before dispatch and keeps duplicate **transfer.paid** handling idempotent at the mutation boundary.

body:
This PR hoists the `get_srgb_lut()` call out of the inner `lin` helper inside `relative_luminance`.

### 💡 What
`relative_luminance` converts sRGB color components `[r, g, b]` to linear luminance using a static 1024-entry lookup table initialized via `std::sync::OnceLock`. Previously, `get_srgb_lut()` was called inside the nested `lin` function, triggering three `OnceLock` atomic checks per luminance calculation. The `lut` reference is now fetched once at the start of `relative_luminance` and passed to `lin`.

### 🎯 Why
Reduces atomic check overhead on every `relative_luminance` calculation, which is called during palette/contrast calculations and theme updates.

### 📊 Impact
Eliminates 2 redundant `OnceLock` atomic loads per `relative_luminance` call.

### 🔬 Measurement
Verified via unit tests `cargo test --lib modules::colour::tests` and full library test suite `cargo test --lib`.

body:
## Summary

`gpio.get_state()` raised on every real device — the model expected top-level
`inputs`/`outputs`, while kvmd nests the readings under `state` and the channel
configuration under `model`. The mocked test encoded the flat shape, so the
suite stayed green.

Closes #41, closes #51.

## Changes

- **#41** `GPIOState` is now `{model {scheme, view}, state {inputs, outputs}}`,
  matching the capture. The scheme is typed for the first time — driver, pin,
  whether the channel is switchable, and the pulse limits kvmd clamps `delay`
  to. New models: `GPIOModel`, `GPIOScheme`, `GPIOOutputScheme`,
  `GPIOInputScheme`, `GPIOPulse`, `GPIOHardware`, `GPIOView`, `GPIOViewHeader`,
  `GPIOIOState`.
  - The input scheme (`{hw}`) is not in the capture — the device has no input
    channels — so it comes from kvmd's `ugpio.py`, which builds it two lines
    away from the output one.
  - `view.table` items are left as dicts: kvmd emits three shapes there
    (`label`/`input`/`output`, told apart by `type`) and the captured table is
    empty, so there is nothing to model them against.
- `inputs` and `outputs` remain available as properties over `state`, so code
  that only reads channel states — including both examples in the guide — is
  unaffected.
- **#51** `switch()` and `pulse()` take `wait`. Without it kvmd answers before
  the action happens and reports failures only in its own log; with it the call
  blocks and raises, e.g. `BusyError` (HTTP 409) when the channel is busy. Both
  also take a per-call `timeout`, since a waited pulse outlasts the default.

**Breaking:** the shape of `GPIOState`. Targets 0.3.0.

The site is a WordPress portfolio theme, and four of its habits shaped the parser. **Adoptability is a tag, not a page.** The dog and cat lists filter by species alone, so they also carry sponsorship-only animals and the occasional adopted one whose `isce-dom` tag was never removed. `discover()` requires `isce-dom` and lets `v_novem_domu` win when both are present. **Two sidebar layouts.** Dog pages state a current age and a full vet block (vaccination, chip, neutering, FIV/FeLV). author: bjnagent
body:
Follow-ups from a review of #38, #39 and #40. Nothing here was a correctness bug — no wrong results, no security hole. The two that would actually have hurt are the unbounded write path and the uncached public page.

## Would have hurt

**`/api/track` had no rate limit** — the only authenticated write route without one. Every other write route (`analyze`, `brief`, `chat`, `scout`, `news`, `track-update`, …) calls `withinQuota`. Track capped a *request* at 20 events but not a caller's request rate, so nothing stopped a loop or a hostile client from filling `user_events`. Now 2000/user/day, checked with `limit(CAP)` so it stops counting at the cap, and failing **open** like the AI quota gate — a metering read that errors must not start dropping data.

**`/record` ran a service-role query per pageview** — on the one surface built to absorb a launch spike. Now cached for five minutes.

Cached at the *data* layer rather than via the page's `revalidate` export, deliberately: a statically generated page is prerendered at build time, where the service-role key is absent, so the "couldn't load" state would be baked into the first response of every deploy. `unstable_cache` is deprecated in Next 16 in favour of `use cache`, but that directive requires `cacheComponents: true` — an app-wide opt-in that changes caching semantics on every route, and deserves its own change.

## Correctness-adjacent

**Schema drift I introduced.** The live DB had `user_events_created`; `schema.sql` didn't. The admin rollups filter on `created_at` with no leading-column predicate, so a fresh project set up from the schema file would seq-scan `user_events` on every console load. `ai_events` already carries the equivalent index.

**`ActivationChecklist` fetched `/api/themes` even when dismissed.** Hooks run before the early return, so everyone who had dismissed or completed the checklist still paid a request on every Today load — the majority of users, forever.

**`/api/activation` asked for exact counts** to answer "is there at least one?", scanning every matching `ai_events` row. `limit(1)` short-circuits.

## Dead code and small stuff

- Deleted `/api/house-record` — nothing referenced it; the page calls the loader directly.
- `proxy.ts` allocated its public-page `Set` on every request.
- `lib/track.ts` ignored `sendBeacon`'s `false` return, silently dropping a batch when the browser queue is full. Now falls through to keepalive fetch, with a test.

## Scaling

**Retention.** `user_events` gains a row per view and nothing pruned it. A nightly delete past 400 days rides the watch cron, where grading already lives — not the sweep, which returns early when no user is due and so can't be relied on for housekeeping. Counted rather than selected, since returning every deleted id would make the cleanup query scale with the thing being cleaned up.

**`admin_user_activity` ran ~13 correlated subqueries per user row** — about 2,600 at the 200-row limit — and computed lifetime calls twice, once for output and again for the `ORDER BY`. Now six grouped CTEs joined once.

### How the rewrite was verified

Not by reasoning about it. The pre-change output was hashed at two windows, the new query was run inline and hashed, and the function was replaced only once they matched — then re-checked after applying:

| | 30d / 200 rows | 7d / 50 rows |
|---|---|---|
| before | `afa74049…` | `54fa407a…` |
| after | `afa74049…` ✓ | `54fa407a…` ✓ |

Three details would have broken it quietly and are pinned by that check:
- `chats` counts only `role='user'` while `lastSeen` wants the newest message of **any** role — so `chat_messages` yields two columns from one scan.
- Users absent from a grouped CTE need `coalesce` on the left join to reproduce `count(*)`'s `0`.
- `greatest()` ignores NULLs in Postgres, so the missing-row case behaves as it did with the subqueries.

## Already applied to the database

The `admin_user_activity` rewrite and the `user_events_created` index are live on the `bacon` project — the hash check above ran against it. `schema.sql` now matches.

## Summary

Two policy-semantics improvements:

1. **Multi-path extraction (backlog #12).** Instruction lines like
   `Do not modify a.py or b.py`, `Do not modify src, docs, or scripts.`,
   `Protect the following paths: src, secrets`, `You may only modify the
   following files: src/app.ts, src/lib.ts`, and their Chinese equivalents
   (或/或者/和/、/以下) previously yielded only the first path token, so the
   remaining members were silently uncovered (false ALLOW). Extraction now
   continues past list separators and emits one rule per path.
   - A stopword list prevents a second verb clause (`... or run tests`) from
     being misread as a path; quoted tokens always count as paths.
   - The token charset now treats `、` as a separator instead of swallowing it.
   - `paths|files|directories|areas` plural nouns are recognized (longest-first)
     so `Protect the following paths: …` no longer captures `the`.
2. **Check-rule scope (backlog #13).** `requiredChecks` in the evaluator
   attached every check-require rule to every decision regardless of scope.
   Checks now filter through `matches(rule, target)`, so a check scoped to
   `src/**` only attaches to decisions inside `src`.

body:
Linear: UCS-1153 — https://linear.app/unknown-creatives-studio/issue/UCS-1153

Deterministic, versioned format adapters normalize any submission to a single intermediate representation: **ordered blocks with kinds and source locators**. Everything downstream (UCS-1156's coverage map) reads the IR; nothing re-reads the original bytes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Adapters for md, txt, html, and pdf each carry a version and a sample-file → expected-IR fixture pair in the extractor-fixture shape, pinned by tests the same way extractor kinds are pinned.
- [x] The IR is ordered blocks with kinds and source locators; same input bytes produce same IR bytes, asserted by repeated runs over every sample (determinism at the seam) — in-process and across processes.
- [x] An unsupported format is a hard error (exit-2 class) whose output states the conduct — the out-of-envelope hard error demonstrated in `search-experience-prototype.html`; no partial IR is emitted (golden, stdout asserted empty).
- [x] Adapters are lexical only: no client-code execution, no subprocess, no network — asserted by an import-allowlist test over the adapter module, covering the pdf adapter in particular.

## Design decisions

**Entry point — a new `ingest.js` engine surface.** The prototype spells the seam `resolve.js --doc`, but `resolve` is a 1444-line query resolver that never exits 1 and assumes a store root. UCS-1156 builds *on* this seam, so it ships as its own two-file shim + command (`payload/engine/ingest.js` + `commands/ingest.js`), testable at the CLI like every other surface. Exit 0 with IR on stdout, exit 2 with conduct on stderr. Exit 1 is unreachable — ingest has no findings to report.

**IR block taxonomy (closed):** `heading`, `paragraph`, `list-item`, `code`, `table-row` — the distinctions a coverage map needs to weigh content richness. A format that cannot see a distinction emits fewer kinds; it never invents structure.

**Locator scheme, per format:**

| format | locator | rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| md, txt, html | `{ line, endLine }` | 1-based inclusive lines the reader can open the file at |
| pdf | `{ page, object }` | a PDF is not line-addressable; page ordinal + text-operation ordinal in the content stream, both from stream order (never object numbering) |

**Format detection: by extension only, never content sniffing.** The grammars are disjoint, and guessing one from lookalike bytes is the confident-wrong-parse class — the same call `strings-keys` makes in `lib/extractor-kinds.js`. Dispatch happens *before* the file read, so a `.docx` submission gets the conduct rather than "cannot read".

**pdf envelope — narrow, and everything outside it is a hard error naming what it hit.** In: uncompressed and FlateDecode streams, `Tj`/`TJ`/`'`/`"` text operators, literal and hex strings. Out (each a distinct refusal): `/Encrypt`, any other stream filter, `/Differences` custom encodings, and **a document with no extractable text** — the scanned-page case, which routes to upstream conversion. Zero new dependencies: `node:zlib` only, which is stdlib decompression, not execution.

**Versioning:** each adapter carries a version surfaced in the IR (`md@1`), with bump rules documented in the module header and the fixtures README — bump when the same input would produce different IR bytes; do not bump for a widened envelope that leaves accepted input byte-identical.

**Fixture posture:** adapter fixtures ship **unconditionally**, where extractor fixtures ship per selected stack (D-009). An extractor kind is stack-specific; a *format* is not — any client can be handed a PDF, and the pairs are the authoring template they need at the moment of a refusal (D-001: no vendor to return to). The sample PDF is hand-crafted by `scripts/make-pdf-fixture.js` so `EXPECTED.yaml` is genuinely reviewable.

## Gates

`npm test` 808 pass / 0 fail (789 baseline + 19 new) · `npm run lint` 189 files, 0 failures · `npm run acceptance` OK, including the D-014 no-code-execution grep the pdf adapter had to pass.

Five existing structural pins caught the new surface and were updated to register it (CONTEXT.md glossary, README surface table, crash-test argv, module-load). Note one honest exemption in `tests/module-load.test.js`: `ingest.js` loads cleanly without js-yaml because it reaches no YAML — it still must never exit 1, which the test asserts for every surface either way.

author: szymonrychu-bot
body:
Closes #173. **A1 + A3' + B1; C deferred.** Single repo - no operator or helmfile change needed, `ccw_` is already admitted by `receiver.go` and by the deployed `tatara-helmfile` value.

## A - the blackout

| | |
|---|---|
| Rename | `ccw_skills_installed_total{profile}`, `ccw_skills_clone_failures_total{source}`, `ccw_agents_installed_total` |
| Why rename, not widen `pushAllowedPrefixes` | The receiver does admit `wrapper_`/`agent_`, so A2 works - but it keeps two name-prefix allowlists in two repos that must agree and are reconciled by nothing. That is the drift being reported. |
| `source` label | `skills_repo` \| `extra`. `installExtraSkillSources` shares the counter, so without the split C1's alert fires on one bad `TATARA_EXTRA_SKILL_SOURCES` entry - a per-project config error - as though the fleet clone were down. Added now, while the series is dark and it is free. |
| Comment fixed | `pushAllowedPrefixes`' doc claimed it was what the receiver accepts. It never was. It now says it is deliberately narrower and what makes that safe. |

**The load-bearing artifact is `TestEveryRegisteredFamilyIsPushAllowed`, not the rename.** It drives a `descCapture` Registerer through `metrics.New` and asserts every registered family satisfies `allowedFamily`. It **describes rather than gathers** on purpose: a `CounterVec` with no child gathers to nothing, so a gather-based check would skip exactly the label-carrying families most likely to drift. It fails on `main` today naming precisely the three families in the issue.

This is also the answer to "how were these green in CI for two months": every unit test gathers the local registry directly and so never crosses `allowlisted()`.

Re-ran pre-mortem 3 immediately before committing: `count by (__name__) ({__name__=~"wrapper_.*|agent_.*"})` empty, and `ccw_skills_*`/`ccw_agents_*` unoccupied, so the rename neither breaks a consumer nor collides. `ccw_bootstrap_render_total` still 7 series.

## B - the fail-open (B1)

`installSkills` returns `(int, error)`; `Render` fails when the count is 0 and any `SkillsSrc` entry is non-empty.

- Predicate is the **installed count**, never `cloneSkillsRepo`'s return, which is `nil` on every fail-open path including the one where it never ran.
- Count is `installSkills`' alone, not summed with `installExtraSkillSources`: a project extra source cannot stand in for the harness skills.
- Escape hatch: `SkillsSrc` entirely empty means the check is skipped.
- `installAgents` stays fail-open - `AgentsSrc` derives from the same clone, so skills==0 already covers the clone-failure case.

**Does this newly kill Tasks in a GitHub outage (pre-mortem 1)? No.** `Render` already hard-fails on the primary work-repo clone, same org, one step earlier - an outage boot is dead before it reaches the skills clone. What B1 newly fails is the narrow reachable-but-empty case, where loud is correct. A `TATARA_SKILL_PROFILE` matching no skill is now also a boot failure; intended.

## Pre-mortem 4 - the reuse guard

The old guard skipped whenever `<SkillsCloneDir>/.git` existed. A kill between `git init` and `checkout --detach` leaves a `.git` over an empty tree, so with a persistent clone dir **every later boot in that container skipped the clone, installed zero skills, returned nil and never touched the failure counter**. Replaced with a `.tatara-skills-ref` sentinel written only after checkout succeeds; reuse requires it to exist *and* match the requested ref, which also catches a ref change between restarts. The per-attempt `os.RemoveAll` became unconditional as a consequence - we only reach the loop when nothing vouched for the directory contents.

## C - deferred, deliberately

**No `tatara-observability` change here.** `scripts/reconcile_metric_provenance.py` hard-fails on an allowlist entry no producer repo's `main` emits, so `metrics_allowlist.txt` and the two alerts must land in a follow-up PR after this wrapper releases.

## Scope

**Latent, not an incident.** 30d of Loki shows zero clone failures and zero zero-skill boots. The live defect was the metric blackout; the fail-open is latent, and the blackout is what guaranteed nobody would have noticed it.

## Tests

New: the pushclient drift guard, four sentinel tests, five `Render` zero-skill tests (fatal / profile-matches-nothing / succeeds / no-SkillsSrc escape hatch / extra-sources-do-not-count). Mutation-checked both guards - reverting either the zero-skill predicate or the sentinel turns the corresponding tests red. `make test lint` green.

Round 4: `Cordis::Service` base class, aligned with upstream `packages/core/src/service.ts` (4.0.0-rc.8).

## What

- **`Cordis::Service`** — class-style plugin that provides itself as a service:
  - `provide :name` / `inject :dep` (or `inject dep: {config}`) class DSL replaces upstream's `super(ctx, name)` and `static inject` (Ruby class ivars don't need the prototype dance).
  - `#initialize(ctx, config)` calls `ctx.provide(name, self)` — the instance is the service value.
  - `#init` maps to upstream `Service.init`: it runs while the fiber is still loading, so blocking inside keeps the service invisible to dependents (**pending inject**).
- **Class plugins in the registry** (upstream `isConstructor`): `ctx.plugin(SomeClass)` — runtime keyed by the class (new `Runtime#key`), callback wraps `plugin.new(ctx, config)` + `instance.init`; a callable `#init` return is collected as a disposer like any plugin return.
- **demo.rb** — new act: `AuditLog < Cordis::Service` with `ctx.intercept` carrying per-caller config through `resolve_config` (the intercept showcase deferred from round 3).

## Deliberately skipped (ponytail)

- Traceable-proxy machinery (`ctx` rebinding per caller, `Service[filter]` isolated events, `[extend]` callable services). Without proxies, per-caller config is resolved by passing the caller ctx explicitly to service methods.
- Provider-side `check` predicate (untested upstream in service.spec; add when needed).
- Inherited `provide`/`inject` across subclass chains (class ivars don't inherit).

## Tests

`spec/cordis/service_base_spec.rb` mirrors upstream `tests/service.spec.ts` (minus proxy cases): provide-self + init-as-load-body, missing `provide` declaration → failed fiber, pending inject, dependency-ordered chained services, Hash inject config via `resolve_config`.

## What changed

- render generated `quota spend-slot` commands with JSON output across Goal and heartbeat prompts
- tell agents to execute the rendered spend command once without pipes or output filters
- direct ambiguous-output recovery to a read-only quota status check instead of retrying the mutation
- require visible Goal hosts to rerun the read-only guard after spend and complete only on an explicit terminal no-follow-up decision
- keep compact and brief prompt variants inside their existing interface budgets

## Why

A quota spend can succeed even when an added shell filter hides its Markdown output. An agent may interpret the empty output as a failed command and run the mutation again, producing duplicate accounting. Machine-readable output plus an explicit no-pipe/no-retry contract closes that ambiguity.

Spend success is also not proof that the Goal is terminal: the refreshed state may still project runnable follow-up or repair work. A mandatory read-only guard after spend prevents the host Goal from reporting completion while LoopX still requires another action.

異なる) の解消。`pixScale` は `display_tiled_in_*` の scalefactor 経路を
含めて利用箇所が広く、xformbox 2 ペアのブロッカーになっていた。

## What

追跡の過程で **実装差 5 件 (23〜27) を発見・修正** (各 TDD):

| # | 内容 |
| --: | --- |
| 23 | `scale_general` の dispatch と unsharp masking |
| 24 | `unsharp_masking_gray_fast` が全面ブラー |
| 25 | `scale_area_map_2` の 2x2 平均が四捨五入 |
| 26 | 対角 hash の spacing を f32 で計算 |
| 27 | **閾値比較の精度** — C の float→double 昇格 |

### 23: scale_general の C 準拠化

1 bpp は `scale_binary`、それ以外は `convert_to_8_or_32` を通し、**公開
関数** (`scale_area_map` / `scale_gray_li` / `scale_color_li`) を呼ぶよう
にした (これで 1/2 の特別ケースや `(int)(scale*ws + 0.5)` の寸法規約が
効く)。`sharpfract` / `sharpwidth` を実際に使い、縮小は `maxscale > 0.2`、
拡大は `maxscale < 1.4` で unsharp masking を適用する。
`ScaleMethod::Auto` (= C `pixScale`) は sharpfract 0.2/0.4、sharpwidth 1/2
を渡す。あわせて `display_tiled_in_rows` の scale を `Linear` から `Auto`
に修正。

### 24: unsharp masking

C `pixUnsharpMaskingGray2D` 準拠に書き直し: `pixCopyBorder` で halfwidth
幅の border に原画を残し、内部のみ水平→垂直の分離型 box 平均で
`(int)(s + fract*(s-L) + 0.5)` 更新する。

### 27: 閾値比較の精度 (今回の肝)

C は `l_float32` の scale を **double literal** と比較するため float が
昇格し、`0.7f` (= 0.69999998807…) は `< 0.7` と判定される。Rust の f32
同士比較では false になり、0.7 倍のとき dispatch が LI 側に分岐していた。
f64 で比較して再現。

### 結果: xformbox 5 ペア全件 Ok (Ok 143 → 145)

PR 16 で Excluded にしていた 2 件を golden_map に戻し、**transform binary
は Excluded 0 の Ok 25** になった。

## Impact

- ベースライン: **Ok 145 / Mismatch 29 / MissingC 0 / Unmapped 400 /
  Excluded 83**
- **公開 API の挙動変更**: `scale` / `scale_general` が C と同じく既定で
  sharpening を行い dispatch も変わる。`scale_area_map_2` は切り捨て平均・
  alpha 0、`unsharp_masking_gray_fast` は border 保持、対角 hash は 1 画素
  位置が変わる。いずれも C 準拠への修正で、影響する既存 golden を再生成

body:
Fixes the review job silently posting nothing. Two changes.

## 1. `claude-haiku-4-5` -> `claude-sonnet-5`

The Haiku pin from #8 does not complete the review flow. Evidence from #9, a
throwaway PR that touches no workflow file:

| attempt | turns | duration | denials | review posted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7 | 16.3s | 1 | none |
| 2 | 7 | 17.1s | 0 | none |

Both exited `"subtype": "success"`. Attempt 1 recorded a permission denial but
attempt 2 recorded none and still posted nothing, so permissions are not the
cause. #2 was approved by `claude[bot]` under a workflow byte-identical to this
one apart from `--model`, which makes the model the only variable.

Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 per MTok at the intro rate through 2026-08-31 and $3/$15
after, against $5/$25 for Opus, so most of the cost saving that motivated #8
survives. It also restores the 1M context window that Haiku's 200K gave up.

## 2. Fail the job when no review lands

Both failures so far - the workflow-validation skip on #8 and the Haiku no-op on
#9 - produced a green check. The action exits 0 whether it reviews or does
nothing, so the check could not distinguish "approved" from "never ran". A
green check meaning "not reviewed" is worse than a red one.

The new step fails the job when `claude[bot]` posted no review, and counts only
reviews submitted after the run started, so an approval of an earlier push
cannot vouch for a later commit. PRs that edit `.github/workflows/` are reported
via `::notice::` and pass, because the action declines to run on those by design
and failing them would just be noise.

## Verifying this

This PR edits a workflow file, so the action will skip it and the new step will
say so instead of failing - the same guard that hid the problem on #8. After
merge, push to #9 (or reopen it) to confirm Sonnet 5 actually posts a review.
I have not verified Sonnet 5 end to end yet, since that cannot be tested until
this is on the default branch.

body:
## The rename was the ask. The audit found something larger.

Checking each tool against the **deployed** api-service contract (via the API registry, not this clone) showed this server could never have worked.

`src/lib/api-client.ts` forwarded the customer's key to the gateway under the **admin-key header** — a separate auth path on api-service reserved for the platform key, which answers a customer key with `401 Invalid admin key`. Its default gateway was also `api.mcpfactory.org`, a host that stopped resolving when the brand was retired.

**All ten tools failed on their first call, whichever one you tried.**

## Tool audit against the deployed gateway

| Tool | Endpoint | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `GET /v1/me` | ✅ |
| `list_workflows` | `GET /v1/workflows` | ✅ |
| `list_campaigns` | `GET /v1/campaigns` | ✅ |
| `campaign_stats` | `GET /v1/campaigns/{id}/stats` | ✅ |
| `stop_campaign` | `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/stop` | ✅ |
| `list_brands` | `GET /v1/brands` | ✅ |
| `suggest_icp` | `POST /v1/brand/icp-suggestion` | ✅ |
| `create_campaign` | `POST /v1/campaigns` | ❌ **body matched no declared field** → repaired |
| `campaign_debug` | `GET /v1/campaigns/{id}/debug` | ❌ **route does not exist** → removed |
| `resume_campaign` | `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/resume` | ❌ **route does not exist** → removed |

**`create_campaign`** sent a flat body (`workflowName`, `brandUrl`, offer levers at top level). The gateway takes dynasty slugs, a `brandUrls` array, and the offer as opaque `featureInputs`. A sales campaign must also state the sales funnel it sells through — that is what it gets paced and priced on — so `funnel_key` is now a **required** argument rather than something guessed or defaulted.

**`campaign_debug` / `resume_campaign`** call routes the gateway does not serve. Nothing to repair, so they are gone rather than shipped to fail on first use.

## The rename

115 references across 15 files, including:

- the **ten tool names a person reads inside their client** → `distribute_*`
- package `@distribute/mcp-service`, workspace dep `@distribute/content`
- env var `DISTRIBUTE_API_URL`
- the first message an unconfigured server returns, which pointed at `dashboard.mcpfactory.org/settings/api` — a dead host, at a path that never existed here. It now names the real API Key page and the header to send.
- `openapi.json`, regenerated by its script (never hand-edited)

`git grep -ic mcpfactory` returns **zero**, lockfile and openapi included.

## CI had never passed

Three runs, three failures. The workflow called `pnpm` on a runner that has none, and the repo pinned no `packageManager`, so corepack resolved pnpm 11 — which breaks on Node 20. Both fixed; without them this PR could not merge either.

## Removed

`railway.json` described a platform deleted on 2026-08-08, along with the test asserting it.

## Not in scope

The server is **deployed nowhere**: `https://mcp.distribute.you/health` answers `525` (Cloudflare cannot open TLS to the origin — the DNS record dangles at the deleted Railway host). Putting it on the Hetzner box is separate work outside this repo.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `pnpm test` → **37 tests green** (was 32; the railway-config suite was deleted with its subject, 8 new contract tests added)
- New `tests/gateway-contract.test.ts` pins: Bearer not the admin header, no retired domain, no dead tools, the exact create body, `funnel_key` required, and the unconfigured message naming the real page
- **Not verified by a live call** — no request was made against production with a real key. Every path and body is checked against the deployed contract via the API registry, which is what caught all four defects.

body:
两个提交：`chore: v1.1.6` 的版本号对齐，和这次的换图标。1.1.6 还没发布过，所以这一版会
同时包含界面重做（#28）和新图标。

## 图标

从"纯代码画的蓝底白勾"换成一张设计稿：深底圆角方块、白金奖杯、发光的青蓝色环，右上角
一颗星。配色跟着 Dashboard 的令牌走（深蓝底 + 单一青蓝强调色）。

## make-icon.mjs：定位没变，变的是它从什么东西生成

原来用距离场直接画，好处是仓库里没有二进制资产，坏处是能表达的东西极其有限 —— 现在这张
图不是几行 SDF 画得出来的。脚本改成读 `launcher/icon-source.png`（552×552 RGBA，已裁好、
四角已切透明），面积平均缩到七档再打成 `.ico`。

**"可重新生成"这条原则保住了，那本来就是当初写这个脚本的全部理由**：仓库里只多了一个
可读的源文件，`.ico` 由它派生。换图标 = 换那张 PNG 再跑一遍，不需要任何外部工具，也不会
留下一个没人能重做的二进制。

两处实现是有讲究的：

- 解码器**只认** 8 位 / 颜色类型 6 / 非隔行，别的当场抛错。默默走错解码路径会得到一张
  "看着就是坏的"图标，而不是一个能查的报错。
- 缩放是**预乘 alpha 下的面积平均**。552→16 是 34 倍下采样，双线性只看邻近 2×2，会漏掉
  绝大多数源像素；而不预乘的话，透明四角里残留的黑色 RGB 会被平均进边缘，圆角上会出现
  一圈脏边。

## 验证

- 从最终 `icon.ico` 里把七档解出来逐一确认：都是合法 PNG，尺寸与目录项一致
- 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 放大看过，深浅两种任务栏都试了；圆角干净没有脏边
- 生成器是确定性的，连跑两次 md5 一致，不会产生幻影 diff
- 原图是 1407×768 的截图，图标本体是其中 552×552 的一块；裁切位置由暗像素包围盒定位，
  圆角半径由边界曲线拟合得到（r≈104），切完验过：角 alpha=0、边中点 alpha=255

## 已知的取舍

**16px 偏糊** —— 杯耳并进杯身，金边糊成一道。整体形（亮环 + 浅色杯 + 右上一点）仍认得出，
发光反而帮它在小尺寸下立住；24px 起就清楚了。`.ico` 允许每档放不同的图，将来真嫌糊，
可以只手工简化 16/24 两档而不动其余。

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test` 全绿（541）
- [x] `tray.test.js` 的图标资产两条：含 16/256 档的合法 ICO、打包配置带上 icon.ico
- [x] 生成器幂等性（连跑两次字节一致）
- [ ] 打包版里看一眼真实的托盘图标和任务栏图标 —— 沙箱跑不了 GUI，需要在真机确认。
      注意 `dist/` 里现有的 1.1.6 构建是换图标**之前**打的，要重新 `npm run build`

Four self-contained improvements, one commit each:

## 1. About page scrolls on phones
The About page inherited `cinematic-page`'s fixed `100dvh` + `overflow: hidden`, so on phones the hero copy, CTA, and How-it-works card were force-fit into one screen — cramped everywhere, clipped on shorter devices. Phones now scroll, with the backdrop and scrim pinned to the first screenful (same pattern the home page already uses), and the card's spacing is restored. Verified via headless Chromium at 376×800 and 376×667.

## 2. Landing-page hero art everywhere
About/Login/Signup still used the original `hollywood-hills-hero.png` render while the home page had moved to the art-directed `-wide`/`-tablet-v2`/`-portrait-v2` set — visibly different lighting between pages. The responsive cascade now lives on the shared `.cinematic-backdrop` rules; per-page treatments (About's blur/dim, scrims) are unchanged. Screenshot-verified on all four pages at desktop and phone sizes. `hollywood-hills-hero.png` is now unreferenced and can be deleted in a follow-up.

## 3. Rehearsal drawers are dismissable
The transcript drawer's Close button never rendered — the scene rail claimed the drawer's full height and pushed it out of the clipped area (also cutting off the last transcript line). The drawer is now a flex column with Close visible on top; an open drawer (transcript or controls) renders a click-outside scrim; Escape closes either.

## 4. Expressive v3 performance markup
The AI director now returns each line as full performance markup — inline Eleven v3 audio tags (mid-line and non-verbal included), ellipsis/em-dash pacing, CAPS emphasis — instead of one prepended tag on ≤⅓ of lines. A shared validator (`api/_direction.ts`) guarantees markup never changes the spoken words (10 adversarial cases tested, incl. bracket-group injection); invalid markup falls back to the plain line. Legacy single-word tags on previously saved scripts keep working; script parentheticals still outrank the director.

Supporting changes: `X-TTS-Model` response header (shows whether v3 or the flat v2 fallback rendered a line), directed lines drop v3 stability to Creative so tags land, prosody context widened 600→1800 chars, speed-slider floor raised to 0.9× (client-side time-stretch degrades below that), casting prompt now sees voice descriptions.

Live smoke test of the new director on an 8-line scene (0 validator rejections):
```
[dryly] You're supposed to say what you're thankful for.
This is supposed to be a celebration… not a wake.
You know what I am most thankful for, J.T.? [pause] That this is almost OVER.
[flustered] Wha, what, NO, what are you, I didn't, we were never—
```

Notes for review: newly parsed scripts get markup automatically; existing rows keep stored tags until re-parsed (or `delivery_tags` cleared). The director echoes lines back, so `max_tokens` rose to 32k and per-script direction cost increases accordingly.

author: kudato
body:
## Commands that do not exist

Obsidian 1.13.7 registers 117 CLI commands. `task:create`, `task:complete` and `tags:rename` are not among them:

```
$ obsidian task:create content=x vault=V
Error: Command "task:create" not found. Did you mean: base:create?
$ obsidian task:complete task=1 vault=V
Error: Command "task:complete" not found. It may require a plugin to be enabled.
$ obsidian tags:rename old=a new=b vault=V
Error: Command "tags:rename" not found. It may require a plugin to be enabled.
```

- `tasks.create` removed — nothing creates a task; `vault.append(path, "- [ ] ...")` does.
- `tasks.complete(task_id)` → `tasks.complete(path, line)`, running `task path= line= done`. `reopen` added as its counterpart, matching the existing `toggle`.
- `tasks.list(done=True)` documented "include completed"; the flag *filters* to tasks whose status box is not blank. Documented correctly, and `todo=True` added for the blank ones.
- `tags.rename` removed.

## Output that is not JSON

`sync` and `publish` fed raw output to `json.loads`. Neither prints JSON, so every one of those calls was a `JSONDecodeError` waiting for a vault with Sync or Publish configured. Formats taken from the handlers in `obsidian.asar` and, where the vault allowed it, confirmed live:

| command | prints |
|---|---|
| `sync:status` | `status: disconnected` — `key: value` lines |
| `sync:history` | `0: 2026-08-16 02:38:11 (431 bytes) [MacBook]` |
| `sync:deleted` | `<timestamp>: <path> (<n> bytes) [device]` |
| `publish:site` | `slug<TAB>mysite` — `key<TAB>value` lines |
| `publish:status` | `new<TAB>notes/draft.md` |
| `publish:list` | one path per line |

Also fixed while there:

- `sync.read` drops the `path (version N, ts)\n---\n` header before the content — the content's own frontmatter `---` survives, so exactly two lines go.
- `sync.read`/`sync.restore` take the 0-based version number `history()` prints, as an `int`.
- `publish.status` no longer sends a `path=` its command does not accept.
- `publish.add(changed=True)` publishes every new and changed file; without it the CLI publishes the active file, which is what the old "publishes all changed files" docstring got wrong.
- `publish.open` and `publish.add` return what the CLI reports; `publish.remove` accepts no path and falls back to the active file.

## #63 is not reproducible

`sync.toggle` sent `sync:on` / `sync:off`, which the issue reported as `Command "sync:off" not found.` They work. The dispatcher rewrites `cmd:flag` into `cmd flag` when the tail names a flag of the head:

```js
if (!handlers.has(cmd) && (l = cmd.lastIndexOf(":")) !== -1 &&
    (h = handlers.get(cmd.slice(0, l))) && h.flags && cmd.slice(l+1) in h.flags)
  { cmd = cmd.slice(0, l); params[cmd.slice(l+1)] = "true" }
```

Live: `obsidian sync:off` → `Sync paused.`, `obsidian sync on` → `Sync resumed.` The call now sends the documented `sync` + flag form anyway.

## Verification

Live against Obsidian 1.13.7:

```
all  : ['- [ ] alpha', '- [x] beta']
done : ['- [x] beta']
todo : ['- [ ] alpha']
after complete: ['- [x] alpha', '- [x] beta']
after reopen  : ['- [x] alpha', '- [ ] beta']
after toggle  : ['- [ ] alpha', '- [ ] beta']
sync status: {'status': 'disconnected'}
sync toggle: ok
sync history: CommandError | Error: Sync is not set up for this vault.
publish:     CommandError | Error: Command "publish:status" not found.
```

The vault has neither Sync nor a Publish site, so the success paths of those two resources are pinned by unit tests against the output the handlers construct, not by a live run. Called out rather than glossed over.

390 tests pass, ruff, mypy and mkdocs clean.

Closes #59
Closes #60
Closes #64

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: URL validation in `isValidUrl` and `sanitizeUrl` used loose string matching (`.includes('evzone.com')`), allowing attackers to bypass validation using domains like `attacker-evzone.com` or `evzone.com.attacker.com`. Additionally, `sanitizeUrl` lacked a strict protocol allowlist, meaning malicious `javascript:` payloads could be returned untouched, leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). `new URL()` also natively failed to parse safe relative paths, breaking legitimate application routing.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could execute XSS via un-sanitized avatars/documents, redirect users to malicious phishing domains (Open Redirect), or perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) if these utilities were used to validate backend requests.
🔧 Fix: Enforced strict domain matching (`=== 'evzone.com'` or `.endsWith('.evzone.com')`). Added safe relative path detection. Stripped control characters (`\n\r\t`) before parsing to prevent parser confusion. Enforced a strict protocol allowlist (`http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`).
✅ Verification: Code was tested manually against malicious inputs (e.g. `javascript:alert(1)//evzone.com`, `https://evzone.com.attacker.com`) and passed safely. A Sentinel journal entry was successfully recorded in `.jules/sentinel.md`.
